brief.goal: On the locked-test sessions of the 100-session B0 corpus, measure whether a learned head beats the native gate (with and without packaged floors) at predicting the rows that will be NVMe misses at demand, at equal reads per layer, and record a plain advance / do-not-advance verdict against the B2 bar in DSV41_REFERENCE.
criteria: `b1_dataset.py` builds per-split, per-horizon (1, 2, 4) shards from the B0 block directories, skipping warm-up forwards and the integrity report's non-tie mismatch cells, and writes a dataset manifest with row, eligible-row and dropped-cell counts per split and horizon.

Every scorer (gate with and without floors, prev, pop, E2, E5) is evaluated through one shared scoring function, so all tables on a split use the same rows, eligible rows and denominators; a test asserts the denominators match across scorers.

No locked-test row is read before selection is frozen: the evaluation entry point refuses `--split locked_test` unless a frozen selection file (chosen config, cuts, model checksums) exists, and the final run records that file's sha256.
PCA, popularity and every fitted statistic are fit on training-split rows only, enforced by the code and checked by a test.

The final run reports, per horizon, locked-test recall, precision and never-candidate recovery at 1/2/3 reads and at the calibrated cuts, per layer, per stratum and pooled (with and without the 19 drive-flagged sessions), plus the dev learning curve at 15/30/60 training sessions for E2 and E5.
The scorer cost (bf16 bytes and CUDA-graph median time for 6 tokens, one layer) is measured on the RTX 5090 under cc-gpu.lock.

A new DSV41_REFERENCE section (33.26) holds the tables, the artifact paths, the commands, and a plain L+1 verdict against the bar in Design §2, including whether a second capture is warranted per the learning-curve rule.
rules: R1: Locked-test sessions are read once, for the final tables. Model and threshold selection use dev and calib only.
R2: PCA and all statistics (popularity, normalisation, frequency weights) are fit on the training split only.
R3: Code moves to divix01 only by push and a private worktree. Runs use PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python and taskset -c 0-63 with OMP_NUM_THREADS.
R4: Never start, stop or touch production. Never read cc-expert-prediction/dsv41-direct-prod.
R5: Do not change the B0 capture format or the capture tools (`b0_*.py`, `residency_capture*.py`, `router_score.py`, `tier_sim.py`). Do not change `llapor.py` or `pca.py`; import them.

Layout: flat scripts in `analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/`, one per stage: `b1_rows.py` (the Group contract and shard I/O), `b1_extract.py`, `b1_dataset.py`, `b1_score.py` (the shared scoring contract and metrics), `b1_baselines.py`, `b1_head.py`, `b1_train.py`, `b1_select.py` (selection file, locked-test guard, learning curve, bootstrap, verdict), `b1_cost.py`, `b1_report.py` and `b1_run.py`. Tests sit beside them as `test_b1_<module>.py`.

Imports copy the `b0_integrity.py` header. Set `HERE`/`REPO`, then `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` for `scripts/dsv41` (tier_sim), `analysis/dsv41-drive/router-capture` (router_score) and HERE, with `# noqa: E402` on the imports that follow. `sglang.*` comes from PYTHONPATH. Tests start with `HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent; sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))`.

Gate math: fp32 `softplus(x @ W[row].T).sqrt() + bias[row]`, with x decoded from bf16 words by `router_score.bf16_to_f32`. Only tokens below the forward's live count are read. Rows with `gate_has_bias` false have no gate scorer. The margin is `score - score[m, 5]` (the token's 6th). The gate's union over tokens is ordered by (-best margin, expert id), as in `layer_cover_oracle.candidate_list` / `verify_replay.Replay.gate_choice`. A learned head aggregates with 1 - prod(1 - p).

Labels: an eligible row is a target route of kind `LaneKind.MISS_GPU` (4) or `MISS_CPU` (5), counted once per (forward, target layer, expert). A row of kind 0 (VRAM hot) is never eligible, and reading one counts as wasted. Every scorer skips hot rows (`fwd['hot'][layer]` from `tier_sim.load_forwards`) and rows the snapshot mask shows in RAM, inside the one shared scoring function, never per scorer.

`b1_dataset.py` also takes the model path (the gates come from `b0_integrity._gates`) and the integrity report path (non-tie mismatches are listed under `per_session[*].mismatches` with seq, layer_id and token). It uses the corpus `manifest.json` for split, flagged, warm_start and session_block, and each block's `rids.json` for rid -> session.

Shards: each split has one x shard per session (uint16 bf16 words [N, 5120]) and per-horizon (1, 2, 4) group shards per session. A Group points into its session's x shard by `x_offset`; x is never copied into a horizon shard. Readers stream shard by shard (np.memmap for x) and never hold the whole corpus. Outputs go to `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/b1-dataset-<date>/` and `b1-run-<date>/`, never the root volume or the repo.

Style: data containers are `msgspec.Struct` (frozen where possible), never `@dataclass`. Prefer pure functions, called by keyword when they take 2+ args. Keep functions under ~100 lines; orchestration reads like pseudocode. Use protected `_helpers`. No defensive getattr/hasattr. CLIs use argparse with `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` and `sys.exit(main())`, and write JSON with `indent=1`.

Comments: ASCII, one or two lines, only facts the code cannot show (units, layouts, the source of magic numbers such as the 0.33-0.52 ms slopes from §33.24). Each module starts with a docstring covering its purpose, inputs and a `Usage:` line. No Args/Returns blocks.
Determinism: all randomness (subsampling, nested learning-curve subsets, init, bootstrap) takes an explicit seed. Seeded CPU runs must give identical results.

Tests: CPU-only and synthetic (`tmp_path`) unless they need CUDA. GPU tests skip when CUDA is absent. The real-corpus smoke is opt-in via `SGLANG_B1_CORPUS` and skips when it is unset. Pytest checks run only as `/Users/dnikolaidis/.hx/checks/divix01-pytest <named test_b1_*.py files> -q -p no:randomly` (add `--gpu` for test_b1_cost.py). The only laptop check is `python3 -m py_compile`. Never write `uv run`, `uv sync` or `pip install`, and never commit `python/uv.lock` or `python/.python-version`.

Docs: DSV41_REFERENCE.md gets a new `### 33.26` section after §33.25 and before `## Sources`, in §33.25's style: a short intro, paths, a rerun command block and result tables. Every number from the post-merge run is `pending` (D7).

items.body:
### 1. Dataset and the scoring contract
- `b1_dataset.py BLOCK_DIR... --manifest M --out D` builds per-split, per-horizon shards once, reusing `b0_integrity.py`'s loaders (route log, router capture, residency snap/label/seq, `rids.json`). Verify forwards with `rids == []` are skipped. Shards live on `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/b1-dataset-<date>/`, never the root volume.
- One row per (verify forward, live token m, source row T, horizon h in {1,2,4}) where the horizon is valid ("invalid: no target row"):
  - source: gate input x[T] (5,120 bf16), source top-6 ids and weights, source layer id, stratum, gate_has_bias;
  - target: layer id, stratum, true top-6 ids, each route's demand kind (label.bin);
  - the residency snapshot's 384-bit RAM mask for the target at prediction time;
  - the target gate on x[T]: its top-12 ids and biased scores (`sqrt(softplus(W x)) + b`, fp32), the gate baseline's and E5's input.
  - identity: session, split, block, seq, rid, warm_start.
- **Eligible row** (the recall denominator): a target route whose demand kind is MISS_GPU or MISS_CPU (`LaneKind` 4/5), counted once per (forward, target layer, expert).
- **Scoring contract, identical for every scorer:** a scorer gives per-token expert scores for the target; the forward's candidates are aggregated over live tokens (the gate keeps today's rule: union of up to k per token, ordered by margin to the token's 6th score; a learned head uses 1 - prod(1 - p) over tokens), rows the snapshot shows in RAM are skipped, and the top `reads` rows per (forward, target layer) are read, for reads = 1, 2, 3, and at score/probability cuts. VRAM-hot rows (kind 0 at demand) are not eligible and a read of one counts as wasted.
- **Metrics per scorer:** recall of eligible rows, precision of rows read, never-candidate misses recovered (eligible rows outside the gate's top-12), expected saving per read priced with the layer-cover slopes (0.33-0.52 ms per last miss), all per layer, per stratum and pooled; plus calibration on the calib split.
- Drive-flagged sessions (19) are kept: labels depend on residency, not drive timing. Every final table also reports the pooled result without them.
- Hot rows at prediction time come from the job trace's per-forward hot set (`tier_sim.load_forwards`, `fwd["hot"][layer]`, as `verify_replay.py` uses it); every scorer skips them.
- The dataset drops the (forward, layer, token) cells the integrity report lists as non-tie mismatches (one: b000 seq 1283, layer 39, token 1) and records the count dropped.
- Memory: rows are streamed from shards; nothing loads the whole corpus. Every process runs under `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0` (or the GPU under cc-gpu.lock).

### 2. Scorers, training and selection
- **Baselines** (`b1_baselines.py`), all through the §1 contract:
  - `gate`: the target layer's native gate on x[T], today's rule; at L+1 with and without the packaged floors (`ram_prefetch_margin_floors.json`, `min_margin` per target row); at L+2/L+4 without floors (they were fit at L+1).
  - `prev`: the same session's previous request verify forward's routes at the target layer, ranked by how many of its tokens routed there.
  - `pop`: per target layer, how often each expert was an eligible row in the training split; a static ranking.
- **E2 head** (`b1_head.py`, `b1_train.py`; adapts `llapor.py`/`pca.py`, not their Qwen constants):
  - features: PCA(x[T]) at rank 256, fit on a training-split subsample of at most 200k rows; the source's 384-wide route mask and 384-wide weights; learned embeddings for source layer, target layer and stratum (16 dims each);
  - a residual MLP (`MiddlePredictor`'s shape) at hidden 512, 384 sigmoid outputs;
  - target: multi-hot of the target's routes that were not VRAM-hot; BCE loss; AdamW, cosine schedule, early stopping on dev eligible-row recall at 1 read.
- **E5 head:** E2 plus the target gate's top-12 biased scores and their margins to the token's 6th score, scattered dense over 384 experts; hard negatives (experts in the gate's top-12 that were not routed) up-weighted in the loss by w in {1, 2, 4}, chosen on dev.
- **Selection:** a small grid on dev only (PCA rank 128/256, hidden 256/512, E5's w); score/probability cuts calibrated on calib. One model per horizon (L+1, L+2, L+4).
- **Learning curve:** E2 and E5 retrained on 25/50/100% of the training sessions (15/30/60, nested, seeded), measured on dev. "Still improving" means the 50->100% step raises dev L+1 precision at 1 read by more than half the 25->50% step.
- **Scorer cost** (`b1_cost.py`, GPU under cc-gpu.lock): the head's bytes in bf16 (PCA projection plus MLP plus embeddings), and its median time over 1,000 runs on 6 tokens for one layer, CUDA-graph captured, against 0.1 ms per layer.
- **Locked test, once:** after selection is frozen, every scorer runs on the 15 locked-test sessions; tables per horizon, per layer, per stratum, pooled, and pooled without drive-flagged sessions; with the per-session paired median and a 95% session-bootstrap interval for head minus gate-with-floors.
- **Verdict (L+1 only):** advance if, at 1 read per layer, precision rises by >= 0.15 over gate-with-floors, or, at the gate-with-floors' precision, eligible-row recall is >= 1.25x; with the bootstrap interval's lower bound above zero, and the scorer within 0.1 ms per layer. Otherwise record that the native gate is the ceiling for same-token L+1 prediction at this budget. L+2/L+4 tables are reported with no bar.
- **Where it runs:** training on the GPU under cc-gpu.lock, cores 32-63 (production is stopped, so the GPU is free); dataset and baselines on cores 0-63 under the 8 GiB cap.

# Track B1+B2: learned L+1..L+4 expert predictor vs the native gate on the B0 corpus

## Goal
On the locked-test sessions of the 100-session B0 corpus, measure whether a learned head beats the native gate (with
and without packaged floors) at predicting the rows that will be NVMe misses at demand, at equal reads per layer, and
record a plain advance / do-not-advance verdict against the B2 bar in DSV41_REFERENCE.

## Acceptance criteria
- `b1_dataset.py` builds per-split, per-horizon (1, 2, 4) shards from the B0 block directories, skipping warm-up forwards and the integrity report's non-tie mismatch cells, and writes a dataset manifest with row, eligible-row and dropped-cell counts per split and horizon.
- Every scorer (gate with and without floors, prev, pop, E2, E5) is evaluated through one shared scoring function, so all tables on a split use the same rows, eligible rows and denominators; a test asserts the denominators match across scorers.
- No locked-test row is read before selection is frozen: the evaluation entry point refuses `--split locked_test` unless a frozen selection file (chosen config, cuts, model checksums) exists, and the final run records that file's sha256.
- PCA, popularity and every fitted statistic are fit on training-split rows only, enforced by the code and checked by a test.
- The final run reports, per horizon, locked-test recall, precision and never-candidate recovery at 1/2/3 reads and at the calibrated cuts, per layer, per stratum and pooled (with and without the 19 drive-flagged sessions), plus the dev learning curve at 15/30/60 training sessions for E2 and E5.
- The scorer cost (bf16 bytes and CUDA-graph median time for 6 tokens, one layer) is measured on the RTX 5090 under cc-gpu.lock.
- A new DSV41_REFERENCE section (33.26) holds the tables, the artifact paths, the commands, and a plain L+1 verdict against the bar in Design §2, including whether a second capture is warranted per the learning-curve rule.

## Decisions
- Corpus: `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/b0-corpus-100-20261012`, 100 sessions, whole-session split train 60 / dev 15 / calib 10 / locked_test 15 (owner decision: 100 sessions, not 300).
- Horizons: the B2 verdict is on L+1 only. The same head code also trains L+2 and L+4 and reports their tables as evidence for the lead-time lever (E3), with no bar applied; L+3 is not trained.
- Head shape: one model per horizon (L+1, L+2, L+4), shared across all source layers, with learned embeddings for source layer, target layer and stratum. Layers where it loses to the gate show in the per-layer tables; no per-pair head is trained in this feature. - The corpus is complete: 100/100 sessions done, 0 failed, 19 drive-flagged, 4 blocks (b000-b003), 16 GB.
- A second, disjoint capture is made only if the head is near the bar and still improving on the learning curve.
- Training runs on the GPU under cc-gpu.lock (cores 32-63); dataset building and baselines run on cores 0-63 under the analysis memory cap (8 GiB, no swap).

- The never-candidate set is "eligible rows outside the target gate's top-12 for every live token of the forward".

- Locked-test sessions are read once, for the final tables; model and threshold selection use dev and calib only.
- PCA and all statistics (popularity, normalisation, frequency weights) are fit on the training split only.
- Code moves to divix01 only by push and a private worktree; PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python; taskset -c 0-63 with OMP_NUM_THREADS.
- Never start, stop or touch production; never read `cc-expert-prediction/dsv41-direct-prod`.

items.body: Shards: each split has one x shard per session (uint16 bf16 words [N, 5120]) and per-horizon (1, 2, 4) group shards per session. tasks.intent: New b1_score.py is the one evaluation function every scorer goes through (C2, S§1.1).
